title: Notion Alternative Open Source Self Hosted: A Practical Field Guide
meta_description: What does Notion Alternative Open Source Self Hosted cost in 2026 (spoiler: nothing), and how do you set it up properly? Covers free tiers, open-source…
intro: If you've been searching for notion alternative open source self hosted, you've probably noticed two kinds of advice: paid tools that open with a soft upsell, and abandoned blog posts that stopped being true years ago. This one is built to stay useful, and it's maintained automatically.

We'll walk through Appflowy, Affine, Activepieces, and N8n Workflow Automation — and finish with the questions people actually ask, so you can check before you buy anything. You shouldn't have to buy anything.

sections.heading: Appflowy
paragraphs: Skip the fluff and start here: AppFlowy is an open-source Notion alternative you can run locally or self-host, free.

So what does that look like when you're actually doing it? Documents, databases, kanban and wiki-style workspaces, with data stored where you choose — local files or your own server. It is the standard answer to 'Notion but open source', and it is genuinely maintained.
Keep it this simple and you'll be ahead of most tutorials out there.

sections.heading: Affine
paragraphs: Skip the fluff and start here: Affine is another open-source Notion/Miro hybrid: documents, edgeless canvas, and self-hosting in the community edition.

In practice that means: It leans into 'everything is a block' and lets the same content be a doc or a whiteboard. Self-hosting runs through Docker Compose, and the community edition's free tier is generous for individuals and small teams.
If you only do one thing today, make it this one.

sections.heading: Activepieces
paragraphs: The short version: Activepieces is an open-source automation platform — a genuine free alternative to Zapier and Make.

So what does that look like when you're actually doing it? You build visual flows or write pieces in TypeScript, and it runs self-hosted under a license that allows free personal and commercial use. Like n8n it turns 'I do this manually twice a week' into a node on a canvas.
Keep it this simple and you'll be ahead of most tutorials out there.

sections.heading: N8n Workflow Automation
paragraphs: Here's the part most people get wrong. n8n is a workflow automation tool in the spirit of Zapier that you can self-host for free.

Which, in day-to-day terms, means: It is fair-code (not strictly open source, which the project is upfront about) and runs entirely on your own machine with a Docker container. The free personal use is unlimited; teams pay only when they outgrow the hobby tier. For a blog it handles the glue: fetch, transform, publish, notify.
No signup wall, no credit card — just a README and some patience.
